note: The action menu from rules v2. The same menu is used by the people and factions the game controls. All invention.

actions.name: Host a feast
actions.success: The guest of honour and the two coolest guests +1 opinion, and the guest of honour's secrets come out.
actions.failure: Guests +1 opinion, and nothing comes out.

actions.name: Grant an office
actions.success: Recipient +2 opinion, and their faction gains the office's power. Anyone else who wanted it gains a grudge.

actions.name: Revoke an office
actions.roll: auto, or a roll if the holder has armed friends
actions.success: The office returns to you. Holder -3 opinion and a grudge, and they are Humiliated.
actions.failure: The holder resists, and there is fighting in the streets.

actions.name: Arrange a marriage
actions.roll: auto if their house agrees (opinion 0 or better)
actions.success: Both houses +2 opinion, a dowry of 1 to 2 silver, and their house is bound to you.

actions.name: Petition for support
actions.roll: a die plus their opinion of you, 4+
actions.success: They speak for you: their faction +1 mood.
actions.failure: Nothing.

actions.name: Bribe
actions.success: +1 opinion per silver. 3 silver also clears one grudge.

actions.name: Pardon
actions.success: Clears a grudge and frees them if held. A plotter rolls to leave the plot.

actions.name: Imprison
actions.success: Held. Removed from any plot. Their faction -1 mood, and -1 power if they lead it.
actions.failure: They flee the city and become a rival (Hunted).

actions.name: Execute
actions.success: Permanent. Their faction -1 power. Their kin gain a grudge, and the nearest may become a rival (Bereaved).

actions.name: Exile
actions.cost: someone held or in the city
actions.success: They leave the city and become a rival (Exiled).

actions.name: Hand out grain
actions.success: The common citizens +1 mood.

actions.name: Give land
actions.success: That faction +1 mood, and its goal is met if land was the goal.

actions.name: Propose a law or levy
actions.roll: an assembly vote: each faction's power counts for or against, then one die
actions.success: The law is in force. The winning side +1 power.
actions.failure: The law fails, and cannot be put again this season.

actions.name: Seize property
actions.success: +2 to 3 silver. The rich families -1 power and -1 mood. The target gains a grudge.
actions.failure: The silver is hidden, but the rich families' mood falls anyway.

actions.name: Strike coin
actions.success: +2 silver, and the rich families -1 mood.

actions.name: Build
actions.success: Citadel (4 silver, defense +2), granary (3 silver, grain lasts longer) or wall (3 silver, +2 against a Carthaginian landing).

actions.name: Pay the guard's arrears
actions.success: Arrears cleared. The guard +1 mood if they were owed for a season or more.

actions.name: Hire mercenaries
actions.success: Guard strength +1 and upkeep +1.

actions.name: Grant land or citizenship to the guard
actions.success: The guard +1 mood, and their goal or agenda is met. The common citizens -1 mood.

actions.name: Disarm the citizens
actions.success: The common citizens -2 power and -2 mood. Their plots lose 2 strength.
actions.failure: Street fighting, and the Carthage clock +1.

actions.name: Raid
actions.success: +2 to 3 silver or grain, and the leader +1 opinion.
actions.failure: Ships or men lost. The Carthage clock +1 if it was a Carthaginian town.

actions.name: March on
actions.success: Take the place.
actions.failure: It becomes a siege: the next march there gets +1.

actions.name: Watch a person
actions.success: See their grudges, plots and agenda. Defense +1 this season if they are in a plot.
actions.failure: Nothing found. On a natural 1 they notice, and their opinion of you falls by 1.

actions.name: Plant a rumor
actions.success: Two people each -1 opinion of the other. If they share a plot, the weaker one leaves it.
actions.failure: Traced back to you: both -1 opinion of you.

actions.name: Turn an informer
actions.success: They report on their plot every season: its stage and members are visible.
actions.failure: Their plot learns someone tried, and they resent it.

actions.name: Force a favor
actions.success: They speak for you: their faction +1 mood, and it votes your way in your next vote.

actions.name: Block
actions.success: Cancels the next action they take.

actions.name: Expose
actions.success: Their secret goes public: influence -2, a grudge, and a political rival drops a rank. With secrets on, exposing a man who tried to blackmail you ends his hold over you, but he tells the city his worst secret about you as a parting shot (about half the harm), and his kin and faction take it ill.

actions.name: Envoy to Carthage
actions.roll: 4+, Silver-tongued +1, a raid on Carthage this year -2
actions.success: The Carthage clock -1.
actions.failure: No change.

actions.name: Buy grain abroad
actions.success: Grain +2.

actions.name: Offer terms to exiles
actions.success: The exile comes home. A rival drops one rank.
actions.failure: They refuse, and a rival gains a rank.

actions.name: Start a plot
actions.cost: a grudge, and a rival rank or an Angry faction
actions.success: A plot at Whispers.

actions.name: Recruit
actions.success: They join.

actions.name: Build a following
actions.success: The agenda step Build a following succeeds.

actions.name: Lend
actions.success: The borrower owes a favor.

actions.name: Muster the army
actions.cost: 2 silver and 2 months of grain (the generalship)
actions.success: An army at Syracuse with two seasons of food: the citizens' levy (if they are not Angry), 1 from each allied city of yours with men to spare, your household, and the guard if you take it. A guard in the field does not defend you at home.

actions.name: Send the army
actions.cost: the army's march for this season (the generalship)
actions.success: It marches up to 20 days along the roads (10 in winter), and stops if an enemy army bars the way. Against a hostile city it lays siege; a town without walls opens its gates to a much larger army. You choose now whether a city that falls is spared or sacked.

actions.name: Storm the walls
actions.cost: the army's assault for this season
actions.roll: 4+, strength / 3, siege lines up to +2, engines +1, the walls -2 each, its defenders
actions.success: The city is yours, spared or sacked as you ordered.
actions.failure: Thrown back: the army loses a sixth of its men.

actions.name: Forage
actions.success: One more season of food (three at most). The town loses 2 months of grain and leans further against you.

actions.name: Disband the army
actions.success: The men go home and the guard is back at your door. Mercenaries lost in the field are gone from the guard.

actions.name: Embassy to a city
actions.roll: 5+, its lean, its fear of you, your army or Carthage's nearby
actions.success: The city becomes your ally: it pays you silver in summer and sends men when you muster. A tribute town that joins you raises Carthage's anger.
actions.failure: Nothing.

actions.name: Declare war on Carthage
actions.success: War. Carthage's anger goes to 10, and the tribute towns lean your way.

actions.name: Accept Carthage's terms
actions.success: Peace: each side keeps what it holds, Carthage's army goes home, and its anger falls to 4.

actions.name: Seat a counsellor
actions.success: He takes a seat at your council and speaks before each of your actions: his opinion of you +1, and the seat adds 1 to his influence. The man he replaces thinks 1 less of you.

actions.name: Pay his servants
actions.success: Learn one secret from his household: what he did, not only what he is doing now. A small secret is used up when you use it; a deadly one is a hold you can use again after it rests.
actions.failure: Nothing. On a natural 1 he finds out: his opinion of you falls by 1, and he knows a secret about you.

actions.name: Buy back a secret
actions.cost: 1 silver, plus 1 for each small secret he holds over you and 2 for each deadly one
actions.roll: 3+, Greedy +2, Wealthy -1, a grudge against you -1, a Pretender -2
actions.success: He forgets what he knows about you, and any demand he made is withdrawn. Only men you know hold something can be bought: those who made a demand, told the city, or were overheard by your watchers.
actions.failure: He will not sell. You keep your silver, but he thinks less of you (opinion -1).

actions.name: Demand his office
actions.cost: a deadly secret over him (it rests 2 seasons)
actions.success: He hands you one of his offices rather than have the secret told. He holds a grudge, and knows you blackmailed him.

actions.name: Send grain to the army by sea
actions.cost: 2 months of grain and 1 silver to the contractor
actions.roll: auto; at war Carthage's ships may catch it
actions.success: A convoy sails now and lands next season where the army is, if it is on the coast: food for 2 more seasons (3 at most). You choose which rich house runs it.

actions.name: Audit the grain contracts
actions.success: Learn whether a contractor skimmed your convoys. A cheat repays what he kept, pays a fine of 1 silver and is barred. Either way the rich families resent it (mood -1).

actions.name: Give a dinner
actions.cost: 1 silver (2 if the wine is strong)
actions.roll: none: the evening goes where the guests take it
actions.success: The man on the couch beside yours gains standing and thinks better of you; the man who held it before may take it badly. Each part of the evening (the meal, the libations, the drinking) can bring one moment from the guests you chose: friendships, quarrels, a secret let slip, a fight over the couch. Strong wine makes quarrels and slips likelier. Friends from your table plot together more easily; men who quarrelled there never do.

actions.name: Send spies to a town
actions.success: Learn whether a town's first man, or an elder of Carthage, hides something. A secret over a town's first man adds 2 to your next embassy there; over an elder, 1 to your next envoy to Carthage.
actions.failure: Nothing.

actions.name: Begin a great work
actions.cost: one action now; from next season, silver (and food) every season until it is done
actions.success: Work begins with the labour you choose. Peasants are free but miss the summer harvest and resent it; hired men cost silver; craftsmen of your cities anger your allies; craftsmen from Carthage's lands go a season faster and anger Carthage. Unpaid men down tools, and after two seasons unpaid a season's work is lost. At most two works at once. A halted work can be taken up again.

actions.name: Set a man over the works
actions.success: Yourself: one action fewer every season while it lasts, but it goes a season faster and the citizens love you for it when it is done. A man: his faction warms to you, he thinks better of you, and he gains standing when it is done. A man who is no friend of yours skims the silver: the accounts come up short, but they do not say who took it.

actions.name: Halt a great work
actions.success: The work stops and costs nothing more. What is built stands, and can be taken up again later.

actions.name: Write to a faction
actions.cost: none, but the city hears of it
actions.roll: 4+; a follower of their own +1, angry with the ruler +1, loyal to him -1, your letters expected -1
actions.success: They long for you more: their mood toward you +1. Either way the ruler hears more of you.
actions.failure: Nothing comes of it. On a 1 the letter is carried to the ruler, and he hears much more of you.

actions.name: Spread word against the ruler
actions.cost: none, but the city hears of it
actions.roll: 4+; they long for you +1, your sworn men spread it +1, Loyal to him -1
actions.success: A faction thinks less of the ruler: its mood toward him -1. A faction that longs for you and is Angry or worse with him rises for you when you strike.
actions.failure: The stories find no ears.

actions.name: Hire men
actions.success: A company joins you (two among the Campanians). More than two companies cost 1 silver a season for every two; unpaid, they drift away. The ruler hears of it.

actions.name: Buy arms for the citizens
actions.success: Suits of armour wait for the citizens, as Dion's five thousand did. When you strike for the city, the citizens add 2 if they are Uneasy with you or better.

actions.name: Raid Carthage's lands
actions.roll: 4+, +1 for each company beyond two (at most +2)
actions.success: Plunder: 2 silver, and the citizens think better of you (mood +1, at most once a year), as the Sicilian Greeks praised the exiled Hermocrates. Carthage's anger rises 1, and the ruler hears of it.
actions.failure: Your men are beaten off: you lose a company.

actions.name: Win a friend inside the city
actions.roll: 4+; their opinion of you, Greedy +1, holds an office -1, your letters expected -1
actions.success: Sworn to you: when you strike for the city they add 1 (2 for the holder of the citadel or a man of the guard). At most three sworn friends.
actions.failure: No promise. On a 1 your letter goes to the ruler, who hears much more of you.

actions.name: Seek a patron abroad
actions.cost: one action; each patron helps once
actions.success: Silver, hired men or both, at a price that each patron names before you ask.

actions.name: Lie low
actions.success: The ruler hears 2 less of you, and men hunting you lose a step (three times for each hunt at most: after that they know your habits).

actions.name: Seek another refuge
actions.cost: one action (1 silver for the crossing to Italy)
actions.success: You move. Men hunting you lose your trail (once they have named you, they only lose a step), and the ruler hears 1 less of you. Each refuge differs in safety, men for hire and distance from Syracuse.

actions.name: Strike for Syracuse
actions.cost: one action, and everything you have
actions.roll: 4+ with every modifier shown before you go
actions.success: 4 or more: you take the city back. Its ruler is taken or flees.
actions.failure: 2 or 3: you are thrown back and lose half your men. 1 or less: you die in the streets, as Hermocrates did. The odds of each are shown before you commit.
